highlights.title: VSCO Is Gunning for Adobe Lightroom With Its New Desktop App
highlights.summary: The new Studio Pro Desktop app for macOS delivers fast batch editing, RAW support, and more than 200 presets, though a few pro tools are still missing.
body: New photographers looking for inspiration often start with an app like VSCO. The popular mobile app, launched more than a decade ago, is known for one-click presets that emulate film and make it easy to elevate a photograph before posting it to social media. But as newbie shutterbugs level up their craft, they often graduate to an app like Adobe Lightroom and its more professional tool set.

VSCO's pitch is simple: Keep photographers in the ecosystem by building a desktop app to rival Lightroom. On Tuesday, the company announced that its Studio Pro Desktop app is officially landing on macOS, following the launch of Studio Pro on iOS earlier this year. Neither version is available on Android or Windows, though the San Francisco–based company plans to port the apps in the future.

“We're helping shape these folks in their formative years,” VSCO CEO Eric Wittman tells WIRED. “We've got to keep giving them more bricks to build upon their own personal, creative journey—not just their creative journey, but also help them build a career.”

highlights.summary: Rising star Arthur Fils claims his first career win at the ATP Finals by battling to a comeback victory over Rafael Jodar to remain in contention in Turin.
body: Fils, 22, beat 20-year-old Jodar 4-6 6-2 6-2 to become the first Frenchman to record an ATP Finals victory since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011.

It was the youngest match by combined age at the season-ending tournament - which features the eight top-performing men - since a 21-year-old Novak Djokovic defeated a 20-year-old Juan Martin del Potro in 2008.
Fils has risen to a career-high ranking of seventh in the world during a season in which he became the youngest French ATP Masters 1000 champion in Cincinnati.
All four debutants at this year's tournament lost their opening match, with Fils beaten by American third seed Ben Shelton and Spain's Jodar losing to Alexander Zverev in the John McEnroe Group.

highlights.summary: Dr. John H. Powers III was appointed director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a powerful post held for decades by Dr. Anthony Fauci.
body: Dr. John H. Powers III was appointed on Monday to lead the National Institutes of Health division on infectious diseases, giving him control of a politically contentious agency with a budget of over $6.5 billion and responsibility for research into such pressing threats as measles and Ebola.

His designation as director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, a position held for nearly four decades by Dr. Anthony S. Fauci, caps a rapid rise for Dr. Powers, who until recently was an N.I.H. contractor and clinical trials design specialist.

Since the start of the second Trump administration, Dr. Powers gained influence among senior health officials as he was tapped to study vaccine injuries, a priority of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Early last year, Dr. Powers worked with Dr. Matthew Memoli, the No. 2 official at the N.I.H. and a critic of Covid vaccine mandates, to obtain sets of data related to vaccines and autism from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, according to emails reviewed by The New York Times.

highlights.title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
highlights.summary: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design. The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot.
body: The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road.

As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity.

highlights.title: Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI?
highlights.summary: The French CEO of Hugging Face, a mega-hub of open-source AI software, says the attack by OpenAI models earlier this year proved one thing: Humanity can’t let AI be controlled by the few.
body: Clément Delangue, CEO of the open-source AI company Hugging Face, may go down in history as one of the first people ever attacked by a rogue AI agent. His company, which hosts millions of AI models and datasets, was breached in July when hundreds of agents being tested by OpenAI broke free from their sandbox and went on a hacking spree.

As the agents worked at superhuman speed to probe and exploit systems, Hugging Face confronted a bewildering deluge of data. The company’s engineers were only able to analyze the attack by using an open-weight model called GLM 5.2 from a Chinese company called Z.ai.

Delangue moved to the US more than a decade ago, “barely speaking English,” and built Hugging Face into a platform that supports tens of millions of AI developers. The fresh-faced Frenchman, who dresses even more like a skater than most AI execs, says the summer attack highlighted the value of open-weight models, which unlike ChatGPT or Claude can be downloaded and run by anyone.

South Africa Rugby has exercised its right to request a full misconduct hearing, issuing a statement to outline how it had “requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualize his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives”.

Chandra and Ajani are planeswalkers with the power to traverse Magic’s multiverse. The journey to different worlds will be depicted through different animation styles chosen through close collaboration between Netflix, animation studio Digic, and Wizards.

highlights.title: Measles Is Officially Back in the United States. What Now?
highlights.summary: A patient with a measles rash in Texas last year. The number of cases in the United States this year has topped 5,400, more than double last year’s tally and the highest since 1991, nearly a decade before the country attained elimination status.
body: The United States has returned to a time, until recently unimaginable, when measles is a persistent threat, not just a sporadic one that can easily be snuffed out.

Even with rigorous effort, it is likely to take years to regain measles elimination status, which the country officially lost on Tuesday. In the meantime, Americans will need to embrace strategies, some well worn and some new, to contend with this forgotten menace, more than a dozen experts said in interviews.

Local and state health departments will need more resources to combat outbreaks. Doctors, parents and teachers will need to familiarize themselves with the symptoms, and prepare to quarantine anyone who is unvaccinated and exposed for 21 days. Hospitals will need to prepare for an onslaught of patients infected with a highly contagious virus. Public health officials may need new tools to detect, diagnose and stem outbreaks quickly. And they may need to revise the recommended vaccination schedule to protect the most vulnerable.
“We’re really in kind of a new Wild West of our own making,” said Dr. Christopher Monson, an intensive care pediatrician at the University of Rochester.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang Says He Would Return to Nvidia if Asked
highlights.summary: Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of the company last week after revelations that he had affairs with an employee and a woman linked to Chinese intelligence.
body: Jensen Huang said on Tuesday that he was willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive if its board of directors asked him to do so, in his first public statement since resigning last week.

“I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners and customers for me to return as C.E.O.,” Mr. Huang said. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as C.E.O.”

Mr. Huang resigned from the company he co-founded after he admitted he was unfaithful to his wife. The New York Times has reported that he had an affair with an employee at Nvidia, as well as a businesswoman who U.S. intelligence has determined to be an asset for Chinese intelligence.
Nvidia’s board of directors opened an investigation into Mr. Huang last week, and he resigned four days later.

highlights.title: The Apple Watch’s Live Rewind Can Record and Rewind Spoken Conversations. It’s Pretty Awkward
highlights.summary: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.
body: My wife and I were driving back from a date night. She was talking about a friend's very expensive utility bill, but I had missed the beginning of what she said (I was driving, after all).

Then I remembered: Wait, I can ask Siri to remind me! At a traffic light, I double-tapped the digital crown on the Apple Watch, and Siri's new Live Rewind feature spun back the clock 15 seconds and showed me a transcript of what my wife said.
I sheepishly interrupted her to show her the transcript. “Look!” Her reply? “Why wouldn't you just ask me to repeat myself?” She shrugged at this new Apple Watch capability and continued talking.

A few days later, I was chatting with my brother on my stoop. Once again, I lost focus for a few seconds and remembered to ask Siri to help me recall what my brother said moments ago. But this time, before I excitedly showed my brother the Apple Watch screen, I preemptively said, “Yeah, I know I could just ask you to repeat yourself.” I got a perplexed look back.
points: Live Rewind and Siri Recap can transcribe missed moments and summarize your day—if you don’t mind a little social clumsiness.

highlights.summary: Senegal become the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, while Egypt miss the chance to join them and Nigeria suffer another setback.
body: Senegal became the first side to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after Mozambique secured a 1-0 win away against Ethiopia.
That result means the Teranga Lions, who beat Sudan 4-2 on Monday, are guaranteed a top-two finish in Group J with two rounds of fixtures to play.
Eight more sides, including Morocco, Cameroon and Ivory Coast, could join Patrick Vieira's side in booking a spot at next year's finals as the fourth round of fixtures culminates on Tuesday.
Egypt could have qualified with an away win over Malawi but were held to a goalless draw after an inspired second-half showing from Flames goalkeeper George Chikooka.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

highlights.title: U.S. Loses Its Measles Elimination Status, a Historic Setback for American Health
highlights.summary: The nation was once regarded as a global leader for reining in the highly contagious virus. Now, large outbreaks that sicken thousands could become routine.
body: Measles has come roaring back in the United States, as vaccination rates have fallen and cases of the once-extinguished virus have soared. That backslide has now cost the nation its measles elimination status, after the virus spread uninterrupted for more than a year.

“It’s a giant stain on our reputation,” said Jennifer Nuzzo, director of the Pandemic Center at the Brown University School of Public Health. “Everyone ought to be just utterly disgusted by the willing return back to an age of death and high cost.”

The announcement, made Tuesday by the Pan American Health Organization, ushers in a new era in which major outbreaks could routinely disrupt communities around the nation, sickening thousands of children. It also marks a highly embarrassing reversal for a country that showed the rest of the world it was possible to rein in the wildly contagious virus when it won elimination status in 2000.

highlights.title: Daydream’s new AI agent acts as your personal stylist — and can shop for you, too
highlights.summary: Daydream's new AI shopping agent can remember your style, virtually try on clothes, plan outfits around your wardrobe, track sales, and complete purchases.
body: Can an AI agent serve as your personal stylist? That’s what e-commerce veteran Julie Bornstein’s fashion startup, Daydream, aims to find out.

On Tuesday, the company launched “Daydream Agent,” an AI agent that is described as a personal stylist that can help you plan a look, virtually try on clothes, surface relevant pieces based on your taste, and more.

The idea, the company explains, is to put a personal stylist in everyone’s pocket. This application of AI could be promising, given that early adopters of consumer AI agents like Meta’s Muse have found that online shopping is a key use case.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg recently noted that shopping was a top activity for Muse’s over 10 million users, for instance, and that 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily.

highlights.title: Springboks boss Erasmus given six-game ban
highlights.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has been suspended for six international matches with immediate effect, following the extraordinary comments he made about the officiating of his side’s 21-19 defeat to France.
body: SA Rugby has requested a full hearing in response to the sanction.

Erasmus delivered an outspoken press conference on Monday, during which he suggested officials had missed 17 illegal tackles against his side during the match at the Stade de France. He went as far as questioning whether "manipulation" of the result was behind why those incidents were not picked up.

World Rugby confirmed they had reviewed the comments, and an independent panel had imposed the ban under World Rugby's match official abuse sanction process, which was introduced in July in an attempt to reduce the levels of abuse received by officials by sanctioning comments deemed to have been made with a view to undermining confidence in officials.

A statement from World Rugby said: "The panel determined that the comments suggest that match officials acted with bias/prejudice or deliberately influenced the outcome of a match, and when the conduct is considered as a whole a reasonable person would conclude that the conduct constituted an unacceptable attack on the credibility and competence of the match officials.

highlights.title: Robert Pattinson’s James Bond Will Be ‘an Assassin,’ Director Says
highlights.summary: Director Denis Villeneuve's upcoming James Bond has finally found its 007. On Monday, Amazon MGM Studios announced Robert Pattinson will be donning the tux and wearing the gadget-infused watch as the seventh big-screen Bond.
body: In a new interview with GQ, Villeneuve discussed the qualities that he wants in Bond, and what led him to cast Pattinson. "The first quality is that I need to believe that this man is a killer, because more than a spy, Bond is an assassin," Villeneuve said. "I need that kind of anger deep in the eye. It’s not everybody who has that."

While Pattinson first gained prominence as the sparkly vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight films, he's since found his indie niche as an A24 superstar with roles in movies like The Drama, Primetime, and Good Time, where he played a small-time criminal. He also proved he has the chops to play a spy/killer in Christopher Nolan's Tenet. In short: dude's got range, and definitely possesses that "anger deep in the eye. Villeneuve continued, saying he wants his Bond to have an "unapologetic panache" and to command every room he steps into.

"Someone that has a lot of sensuality as well and that people are attracted to and that someone who expressed some kind of pleasure, someone who has width, sometime who has dark humor, sometimes that has pleasure into being in deep shit, someone who is not afraid to put his hand in the mud," Villeneuve said.

highlights.title: Climate Change Visibility Rises in Mainstream TV and Film, USC Norman Lear Center Study Shows
highlights.summary: Stories about the causes and effects of climate change are on the rise in mainstream TV and film, according to a study released Tuesday by USC Norman Lear Center in partnership with Good Energy.
body: The report tracks how often climate change appears in scripted entertainment, as well as what that looks like on screen. It comes on the heels of the release of eco-comedy “Digger,” which stars Tom Cruise as an eccentric oil magnate who accidentally causes an ecological disaster. The film was a bomb at the box office, by Cruise’s high standard, but the storyline’s focus on climate change got a lot of attention in the promotional campaign leading up to the Warner Bros. film’s U.S. release on Oct. 2.
This new research updates and expands on the 2022 report, “A Glaring Absence,” which analyzed 37,453 scripts from 2016-20 and found 36 climate-related keywords appeared in only 2.8% of them.

This year’s report tracks the original 36 keywords, plus an expanded list of 105, across 35,120 scripts from 2021 to 2024. It also tracks quantitative narrative analysis across 100 climate storylines and qualitative analysis across 30 climate storylines. In general, most of the discussion centers around the destructive impact of climate change rather than causes or efforts to find systemic solutions.

body: Feel free to make this with pork instead of chicken, and cook the meatballs on an outdoor grill when it’s too hot to turn the stove on.

To make the meatballs, combine the garlic, chilli, lemongrass, coriander and mint in a food processor and blitz until very finely minced. Scoop the paste into a large bowl. Add the remaining meatball ingredients to the bowl and mix everything together. The mixture will feel very wet – for easier handling, you can place it in the fridge to firm up; it also helps to moisten your hands with a little oil before shaping.

Form the mixture into balls, using about two tablespoons of the mixture for each meatball. Set them on a tray and place back in the fridge if you’re not cooking them right away. You can make the meatballs a day in advance, or freeze for convenience; just add a few extra minutes of cooking time if cooking from frozen.
To make the dressing, crush the garlic and chilli together using a mortar and pestle. Scrape into a bowl, add the remaining dressing ingredients and stir to dissolve the sugar.

highlights.title: Jensen Huang says he’s willing to return as Nvidia CEO
highlights.summary: Jensen Huang, who resigned as Nvidia's CEO last week, would be willing to return as CEO if the company's board of directors wanted it, he said in a statement reported on by The Wall Street Journal.
body: ‘I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,’ Huang said.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”
Huang resigned on Thursday following reports of two affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and a direct report. CFO Colette Kress was appointed interim CEO.

“I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life,” Huang said. “I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation.”

highlights.title: AI Told These Ex-Google Guys How to Build a Billion-Dollar Weapons Business
highlights.summary: Google and Apple alumni Chad Steelberg and Andy Baynes are applying what they learned running software companies and designing iPhones to manufacturing lethal munitions.
body: When Silicon Valley entrepreneur Chad Steelberg decided he wanted to get involved in the war in Ukraine, he had no idea where to start. So the then CEO of enterprise AI company Veritone did what he knew best: built an artificial intelligence model to help him figure it out. Today, he has proprietary munition and missile designs, several government partnerships, and a defense-as-a-service business valued at more than $1 billion.

Steelberg, alongside fellow Google alumnus and former Apple executive Andy Baynes, says they are trying to break the Russia-Ukraine war “stalemate,” Silicon Valley–style. They believe their experience building and iterating technology quickly can help bring Western weapon manufacturing in line with the rapid innovation cycles seen on the battlefield and beat the “attritional cat-and-mouse technology game” that the war, as Baynes describes it, has become.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.title: ‘Madden’ Review: Nicolas Cage Plays John Madden as the Disheveled Buddha of Football in David O. Russell’s Eccentric Stunt of a Sports Biopic
highlights.summary: "Madden" is a stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines. At times, the film can feel like an extended "Saturday Night Live" sketch played straight. But it’s like an "SNL" sketch shot and edited by Scorsese.
body: Cage dons a jowly fatsuit to play the Oakland Raiders coach-turned-sports commentator. It's two parts impersonation, one part Nicolas Cage kabuki.

You could say that every movie writes its own rules. But you can really say that about a movie in which Nicolas Cage, buried under a jowly fatsuit that makes him look like Jiminy Glick playing John Candy, portrays John Madden, the celebrated coach of the Oakland Raiders in their mean-machine ’70s heyday, who went on to become one of the most unhinged — and influential — TV sports commentators of his era.

“Madden” features one more stylized semi-prosthetic character: the Oakland Raiders’ owner, Al Davis, played by Christian Bale with a shark mouth and slick receding hair and a Jewish goombah accent and a princess-doll wife (an unrecognizable Sienna Miller), all of which makes you think he must be some sort of vicious criminal. But no, Davis is just Madden’s fellow monomaniac (the relentless businessman to Madden’s football artist), and these two sustain a testy friendship even once Madden leaves the team.
points: "Madden" is a stunt biopic on cinematic amphetamines.
At times, the film can feel like an extended "Saturday Night Live" sketch played straight.

body: That said, Sophie could always consider including some sort of barrier, too, says Dee Rettali, co-founder of Fortitude Bakehouse in London: “My mother was an amazing baker, and she always sprinkled a very fine crumble mix [just sugar and flour, no fat] on the bottom of her pie before putting in any fruit. That will then absorb most of the liquid.”

On to the bake itself, and Rettali always pops her tin on a baking stone in the oven, because “it really conducts heat into the bottom of the pie”. Franklin, however, thinks that’s a “slightly unnecessary step”. The reason? “It puts a barrier between the base of the pie and the direct heat.” Instead, he simply slides the tin straight on to a rack in the oven: “It will just cook better.”

Gummy, undercooked pastry can also be avoided simply by baking the pie for a bit longer, Franklin says: “With the exception of my own cookbooks, of course, I never think pie recipes give the right cooking times. Always give yourself an extra 10 minutes.” After all, not every home oven is as hot as it says on the dial. And a large pie, Franklin adds, is going to take at least 40 minutes.

highlights.title: Voyage Labs raises $12 million for a specialized AI travel assistant
highlights.summary: Voyage Labs’ flagship product is called Atlas, meant to work as a personal assistant for your trip-planning, available today in private beta.
body: Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants — you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini, or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can beat the competition.

The company is called Voyage Labs, and on Tuesday it announced $12 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SignalFire and SV Angel. The company plans to use the funding to expand supplier partnerships and grow its engineering team.
“People can use it to plan and book and manage their entire journey, from the time they have an inspiration to the time they come back home,” says co-founder and CEO Manik Gupta.

Atlas is designed to serve as an always-on assistant throughout the planning process, fielding ideas and doing research on every idea that’s raised. The long time horizon means Atlas can tailor recommendations based on weeks of conversation, while also monitoring real-time price fluctuations and ultimately booking flights and hotels.

highlights.title: Peter Storey, Arsenal Double winner and England international, dies aged 81
highlights.summary: Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal from 1965. He got 19 England caps and finished career at Fulham. Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.
body: Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.
Storey, who represented England on 19 occasions from 1971-73, earned respect for his uncompromising approach and versatility, also featuring at right-back.

Storey died in hospital after a short illness, surrounded by his family. Arsenal said: “Everyone at Arsenal is deeply saddened by the passing of 1970-71 Double winner Peter Storey. All our thoughts are with his family and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.”

Born in Surrey, Storey began his career at Arsenal and made his debut shortly after his 20th birthday in 1965. He is fondly remembered by the club’s fans for scoring a stoppage-time penalty in the 1971 FA Cup semi-final against Stoke that forced a replay and kept the Double dream alive.

body: It used to be that companies and scientists with ideas for new drugs couldn’t wait to announce their discoveries at meetings, in preprints and on their websites.

Researchers at the biotechnology firm Alnylam Pharmaceuticals have an unwritten policy: Do not reveal early-stage studies or discuss unpublished data, according to its founding chief executive, Dr. Christoph Westphal.

Jacob Becraft of Strand Therapeutics delays filing for patents to keep his company’s discoveries secret. And he is careful about disclosing his company’s intellectual property and confidential material, even to investors.
Alexis Borisy, a co-founder of Curie.Bio, which helps early-stage biotechs, says he tells scientists to “go dark” — don’t publish, don’t present posters at meetings, don’t even go to meetings.

If I had to pick three of my own, here’s what I’d go with: Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, Rear Window, and Sinners. Or, maybe I’d swap one for First Man because I can never get enough of its tense opening scene, or BlackkKlansman because it’s just so good.

Several big box office films are here, from Obsession and The Super Mario Galaxy Movie to One Battle After Another, Weapons, and the fairly recent 4K Blu-ray launch of the Wachowski sisters’ Speed Racer, to name a handful of examples. You have no excuses not to load up holiday stockings with some fantastic goodies for the cinephile in your life (even if that’s you).
points: Gruv always keeps its proverbial fire hose of deals on movies running with a steady stream throughout the year, but the online seller operated by Universal Pictures is really letting it rip now ahead…
Or, peruse its catalog of $13 films that include more recent blockbuster hits, like The Super Mario Galaxy Movie.
